title: Ricci-flow surgery hypothesis — corpus-grounded test

source.author: Myshko, A.
source.title: МЕТАМОНИЗМ: Онтология настоящего. Процессуальная единица реальности

question: Does this corpus independently support the hypothesis that ontodynamic frustration and transition between processual regimes are structurally comparable to Ricci-flow singularity and surgery?

source_findings.claim: P1 is introduced as the minimally actualized difference and is deliberately left without assumed extension, duration or direction at introduction.
The present continuously resolves its non-identity into the next act; the next act cannot be fully identical to the previous act.
The text refers to orthogonal resolution as having been derived in the previous Chapter 3 from the Prohibition of Indifference as a way of removing frustration of self-identity.
The ontology requires a continuing sequence of actualizations rather than a static stopping state.
The need for three spatial degrees of freedom is explicitly left as a task for a later rigorous mathematical derivation.
Physical correspondence hypotheses require subsequent mathematical formalization; proposed experimental effects are not direct deductions from the ontological axioms.

comparison.candidate_correspondence: ontodynamic frustration / orthogonal transition to a new processual act
supporting_structure: continuation is required rather than absolute stopping
current configuration cannot simply become identical to itself
transition proceeds into a new degree/direction of actualization
frustration is referenced as the condition motivating orthogonal resolution
missing_structure: no characteristic scale identified as Planck scale

forbidden_inferences: ontodynamic frustration is mathematically a Ricci singularity
the text derives a surgery operator
the Planck scale follows from the present text

research_result.reason: The corpus supplies a compatible processual pattern but not the mathematical structures required to test a Ricci-flow/surgery correspondence.
